thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-2041 fired - GPUOOM_RATE spike on pool-west-1 (auto-threshold). 75% of recent allocs failed with CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY; simultaneous evictions observed.

pagerduty: Pager PD-2041 - Severity: P1 - Auto-page to oncall (eng-oncall). Escalation: if not ack in 2m -> next.

alex: acked (oncall). I'm looking. Any customer impact visible?

samira: seeing increased 5xxs for hosted/generate on west region, 10m spike in tail latency. Support ticket count up by 3.

jin: pulling logs from node-23 where most OOMs reported. attaching recent dmesg and inference logs.

jin: ```
[ 12345.678901] nv_mem: GPU 0: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY while allocating 312MB
[ 12345.679002] nv_kill: invoked for process model-server (pid 2145)
[ 12345.679103] kvcache: eviction burst: 1200 entries/sec
```

alex: thanks. Can you check nvidia-smi and pod-level memory usage? If it's node-wide, we may need to drain and move serving traffic.

jin: nvidia-smi snapshot: ```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.13 Driver Version: 525.60.13 |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-40GB   On   | 00000000:65:00.0 Off | N/A  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
| GPU   PID   Type   Process name                GPU Memory Usage            |
| 0     2145  C      model-server                  39210MiB / 40536MiB       |
| 0     3200  C      eval-worker                    1400MiB / 40536MiB       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

oliver: looks like a single process near full VRAM. But the OOMs are transient and we're seeing kvcache churn causing allocation failures across multiple pods. Could be fragmentation or a mem-leak in the latest model rollout.

alex: rollout? Which model version is on pool-west-1?

jin: v2.7.1-canary serving the 70% traffic. Canary started ~9m ago. Canary config uses the new attention kernel + larger kv cache config.

samira: support reporting ~8 customers in west experiencing degraded responses; 2 retries escalated to 502. Need mitigation to stop customer impact quickly.

alex: mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to v2.7.0, 2) route traffic off pool-west-1 to pool-east-2 warm standby, 3) reduce model cache size via runtime flags, 4) hot-restart model processes on affected nodes. Which is fastest?

jin: fastest is routing traffic away + draining node-23. Rolling back requires CI gating and may take 10+ min. Drain + fallback should cut customer errors ASAP.

oliver: I'll take ownership of the fallback route. Alex, can you initiate drain on node-23 and mark pool as restricted for autoscheduler? Samira please notify support and post a status. Jin, gather core dumps and logs for root cause.

alex: running command: ```
kubectl cordon node-23 && kubectl drain node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```

alex: cordon done. Starting drain now. Moving 4 model-server pods off the node.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PD-2041 acknowledged by alex at 1749998895.

jin: capturing core files: ```
gcore 2145 && scp /var/crash/core.model-server.2145 s3://redwood-debug/core-1749998888/
```

samira: support update -> Posted to customers: "We detected GPU memory instability in west region; traffic is being routed to alternate capacity. Some requests may see slightly higher latency. We're investigating and will follow up."

oliver: started route change: updating smart-router policy to prefer pool-east-2 for generate endpoints at 80% for 10m. Pushing policy now.

incident-bot: Router change event: policy-update(id=ru-803) applied. New route weights: pool-east-2=80%, pool-west-1=20%

alex: drain is progressing. 3 pods terminated gracefully, one took longer but is now restarted on node-45. Memory pressure on node-23 decreased from 97% -> 42% after evict.

jin: posting a short snippet from model logs showing repeated allocator failures before OOM: ```
[WARN] allocator.cpp: failed_alloc(size=33554432) -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[INFO] kv_cache: evicted prefix=client-98 count=120
[ERROR] model-server: internal allocator retry 3/5
```

oliver: good. Next steps: keep traffic rerouted for 15m, collect metrics for KV eviction rate, confirm rollback only if we see continued OOM after routing. Also open a postmortem ticket and assign to jin+infra.

samira: support: customers notified, CS has an internal note template. I'll escalate for any billing/SLAs if errors persist.

pagerduty: PD-2041 status: acknowledged -> in progress. Escalation timer paused.

alex: quick temp tweak: reducing runtime kv-cache to 0.8x for canary processes to reduce footprint. Command: ```
redwoodctl model update-config --pool pool-west-1 --model canary-v2.7.1 --kv-factor 0.8
```

jin: applied kv-factor change to canary pods in pool-west-1. Observed per-pod mem drop ~1.2GB. Eviction rate down ~60% in last 2 min.

oliver: monitoring: 5xxs dropping to baseline, tail latency slowly recovering. Keep router policy in effect. After 15m, if stable, we can bring pool-west-1 weight to 50% then back to normal.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PD-2041 resolved for now; no active pages. Close after follow-up actions assigned.

alex: creating follow-up issue: infra/7542 - "Investigate KV-cache churn + canary v2.7.1 memory pattern". Assigning jin (owner) and oliver (sre). Samira will add customer impact notes.

samira: added customer impact: ~8 customers with transient 502s, 0 data loss, estimated impact window 9:12-9:34 UTC.

jin: attaching logs and core link: s3://redwood-debug/core-1749998888/, and Grafana dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/metrics/pool-west-1-oom?from=1749998800&to=1749999500

oliver: action items: 1) postmortem in 48h, 2) add a safety throttle on kvcache growth, 3) add health-check that detects sustained allocator failures and triggers immediate routing to standby.

alex: handing off to afternoon oncall (samira) at 1749999480 - leaving notes in oncall-runbook.

samira: acknowledged handoff. Will monitor for 30m and update postmortem. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Notified customers: CS-#4127, CS-#4128.

incident-bot: thread closed by alex at 1749999488.
